legend: Mount ICPC can be represented as a grid of R%%ZSMJ0%% rows (numbered from 1%%ZSMJ1%% to R%%ZSMJ2%%) and C%%ZSMJ3%% columns (numbered from 1%%ZSMJ4%% to C%%ZSMJ5%%). The cell located at row r%%ZSMJ6%% and column c%%ZSMJ7%% is denoted as (r,c)%%ZSMJ8%% and has a height of Hr,c%%ZSMJ9%%. Two cells are adjacent to each other if they share a side. Formally, (r,c)%%ZSMJ10%% is adjacent to (r−1,c)%%ZSMJ11%%, (r+1,c)%%ZSMJ12%%, (r,c−1)%%ZSMJ13%%, and (r,c+1)%%ZSMJ14%%, if any exists.

You can move only between adjacent cells, and each move comes with a penalty. With an aura of an odd positive integer X%%ZSMJ15%%, moving from a cell with height h1%%ZSMJ16%% to a cell with height h2%%ZSMJ17%% gives you a penalty of (h1−h2)X%%ZSMJ18%%. Note that the penalty can be negative.

You want to answer Q%%ZSMJ19%% independent scenarios. In each scenario, you start at the starting cell (Rs,Cs)%%ZSMJ20%% and you want to go to the destination cell (Rf,Cf)%%ZSMJ21%% with minimum total penalty. In some scenarios, the total penalty might become arbitrarily small; such a scenario is called invalid. Find the minimum total penalty to move from the starting cell to the destination cell, or determine if the scenario is invalid.
input: The first line consists of three integers R%%ZSMJ22%% C%%ZSMJ23%% X%%ZSMJ24%% (1≤R,C≤1000;1≤X≤9;X%%ZSMJ25%% is an odd integer).

Each of the next R%%ZSMJ26%% lines consists of a string Hr%%ZSMJ27%% of length C%%ZSMJ28%%. Each character in Hr%%ZSMJ29%% is a number from 0 to 9. The c%%ZSMJ30%%-th character of Hr%%ZSMJ31%% represents the height of cell (r,c)%%ZSMJ32%%, or Hr,c%%ZSMJ33%%.
The next line consists of an integer Q%%ZSMJ34%% (1≤Q≤100000)%%ZSMJ35%%.
Each of the next Q%%ZSMJ36%% lines consists of four integers Rs%%ZSMJ37%% Cs%%ZSMJ38%% Rf%%ZSMJ39%% Cf%%ZSMJ40%% (1≤Rs,Rf≤R;1≤Cs,Cf≤C%%ZSMJ41%%).
output: For each scenario, output the following in a single line. If the scenario is invalid, output INVALID. Otherwise, output a single integer representing the minimum total penalty to move from the starting cell to the destination cell.
note: For the first scenario, one of the solutions is to move as follows: (1,1)→(2,1)→(3,1)→(3,2)→(3,3)→(3,4)%%ZSMJ42%%. The total penalty of this solution is (3−4)1+(4−3)1+(3−6)1+(6−8)1+(8−1)1=2%%ZSMJ43%%.

For the first scenario, the cycle (1,1)→(2,1)→(2,2)→(1,2)→(1,1)%%ZSMJ44%% has a penalty of (1−2)5+(2−0)5+(0−9)5+(9−1)5=−26250%%ZSMJ45%%. You can keep repeating this cycle to make your total penalty arbitrarily small. Similarly, for the second scenario, you can move to (1,1)%%ZSMJ46%% first, then repeat the same cycle.
